subject: Incorporating an individual time-varying covariate in capture-recapture

messages.author: bfa4a88c8a5bc54e
messages.subject: Incorporating an individual time-varying covariate in capture-recapture
parts:
Dear nimble users,

We are currently working on a disease-structured multistate capture-recapture model incorporating pathogen load. The model has three ecological states (alive and uninfected, alive and infected, and dead), and during every survey, multiple samples are collected to determine the probability of detecting infection. So, the 2-D capture history of individual * survey is now 3-D, with individual * survey * sample (y[i,t,k]). The ecological and observation processes are standard CJS model, but there's an additional pathogen detection component as follows (ecological and observation process omitted for brevity):

for(i in 1:n.ind){

   for(t in first[i]:n.survey){

      for(k in 1:n.sample){

         # Pathogen detection matrix

         # Recaptured, uninfected

         TPM.d[1,1,i,t] <- 1  # Infection not detected

         TPM.d[1,2,i,t] <- 0  # Infection detected

         TPM.d[1,3,i,t] <- 0  # Not sampled 

         # Recaptured, infected 

         TPM.d[2,1,i,t] <- 1 - delta[i,t]  # Infection not detected

         TPM.d[2,2,i,t] <- delta[i,t]       # Infection detected

         TPM.d[2,3,i,t] <- 0                  # Not sampled

         # Not recaptured

         TPM.d[3,1,i,t] <- 0  # Infection not detected

         TPM.d[3,2,i,t] <- 0  # Infection detected

         TPM.d[3,3,i,t] <- 1  # Not sampled

         # Likelihood

         y[i,t,k] ~ dcat(TPM.d[o[i,t],1:3,i,t])

      }

   }

}

Ideally, we want to estimate delta[i,t], and also the survival probability of infected individuals phiI[i,t], as a function of that individual's pathogen load (m[i,t]) as follows:

for(i in 1:n.ind){

   for(t in first[i]:n.survey){

      delta[i,t] <- 1 - (1 - delta.r) ^ m[i,t] # Royle & Nichols (2003)

   }

   for(t in first[i]:(n.survey - 1){

      logit(phiI[i,t]) <- phiI.alpha + phiI.beta * m[i,t]

   }

}

Now, in order to estimate m[i,t], we intend to use the pathogen loads of the replicate samples (x[i,t,k]), and then have the individual pathogen loads (m[i,t]) drawn from a population mean mu. There will be mostly NAs in x[i,t,k] because there are only values for individuals that 1) were infected and 2) had these infection detected on a sample.

for(i in 1:n.ind){

   for(t in first[i]:n.survey){

      m[i,t] ~ dnorm(mu, sd = mu.sigma)

      for(k in 1:n.sample){      

         x[i,t,k] ~ dnorm(m[i,t], sd = m.sigma)

      }

   }

}

It turns out that in our simulations, the model runs fine without pathogen loads but not with pathogen loads. We’ve tried varying formulations, including the following, to attempt to only draw infection loads for individuals the model thinks are infected:

m[i,t] ~ dnorm(mu * equals(o[i,t], 2), sd = mu.sigma * equals(o[i,t], 2) + 0.01)

x[i,t,k] ~ dnorm(m[i,t] * equals(y[i,t,k], 2), sd = m.sigma * equals(y[i,t,k], 2) + 0.01)

Even though the estimates of mu, mu.sigma, and m.sigma match the input parameters for our simulations with this last model formulation, the parameters of the capture-recapture model are not recovered properly. Again, omitting the pathogen loads allows all parameters of the capture-recapture to be recovered. (By the way, without the equals() functions in the pathogen load part of the model, mu, mu.sigma, and m.sigma are not recovered properly).

We’re not exactly sure what’s going on here, but we suspect it may have something to do with the dependence of pathogen load on the observed states, and the parameters of the capture-recapture model being dependent on the pathogen load. However, without including the equals() functions when drawing sample and individual pathogen loads, the pathogen load parameters don’t get recovered. Is there something fundamentally wrong with our formulation? That also seems like an an option, because we only observe pathogen loads of a subset of individuals (those that are infected and have infections picked up by a sample).

Looking forward to any thoughts on our problem. We have full code to simulate data and analyze these datasets with and without pathogen loads.

Kind regards,

Matt

messages.author: af31ce3a70c4aa9e
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating an individual time-varying covariate in capture-recapture
parts:
Hi Matt,

See attached for a simulation and analysis that more or less works. It's kind of an N-mixture model for the pathogen load, kind of a CJS for the capture-recapture, with elements from Madeleine Lohman's really excellent recent paper using a robust design in a Bayesian framework. I wrote it in JAGS for now, should be easy to switch, and you could certainly shorten run time by indexing more thoughtfully over the y's, marginalizing, etc... 

Hard to tell what's wrong with your simulation with partial code, could be a few different issues. I'm a bit skeptical of the delta.r parameter. Is this the detection probability of a single viral particle? That's how I simulated it too, but feels like we're boldly crossing the line between incorporating uncertainty and adding inanity. This could get really messy with real data. Additionally, since m is a true 0 for most individuals and it's normally distributed in your model, you're potentially raising 1 - delta.r to a negative value? I'm confused there. I think there is some more thinking to do about exactly how to formulate this. Viral load certainly needs to be a zero-inflated distribution of some kind conditional on infection, and it seems what you sent isn't quite there.

Anyway, see attached. Good luck, seems like an extremely interesting problem with a number of potential solutions! I'll be very interested to see what you end up with!

Thomas
